[Project overview]{.eyebrow}

::: {.lead}
We use nanopore sequencing, a long-read technology recognized as Method of the
Year 2022 by *Nature Methods*, to characterize pathogens and the environmental
reservoir of antibiotic resistance.
:::

These methods let us better understand the environmental reservoir of antibiotic
resistance in Alaska. Alongside the Alaska work, the lab contributed to a global
consortium, the MinION Analysis and Reference Consortium, over the course of
several years. We developed and applied standardized sampling methods and
sequencing protocols to investigate microbial life in 11 rivers across three
continents.

We have also applied our nanopore expertise to advancing scientific capacity for
genomics-based biosurveillance of emerging African swine fever virus and
coinfections in Ukraine.

::: {.horizon-rule}
